title: Affordable housing tax discount and paramedic budget
subtitle: Also WSIB costs for first responders, graffiti options, cleaning audit and IT service profile.
overview: The committee recommended that Guelph adopt an optional property tax subclass for affordable rental housing, with a 35 per cent discount to be confirmed in the 2026 tax policy {{vote:m5}}. It would apply only to units covered by an agreement with a level of government. Staff could not say how many units will qualify, so councillors asked for a scenario memo before Council votes at the end of the month.

The committee also recommended a $1,300,000 in-year increase to paramedic compensation and several capital budget changes, including earlier funding for ambulances and electric bus charging {{vote:m4}}. It received a report on rising WSIB costs for fire and paramedic services {{vote:m1}} and received a value for money audit of facilities cleaning {{vote:m3}}.

Separately, the committee directed staff to report on graffiti options by the end of the first quarter of 2026, including volunteer, mural, education and private-property removal ideas {{vote:m2}}. Councillors also heard an IT service profile. The Chief Administrative Officer responded to an opinion piece about South Hampton Street road work, saying staff had met with the residents concerned.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended adopting the optional affordable rental subclass for multi-residential property classes from January 1, 2026, with a 35 per cent discount to be set in spring 2026 tax policy {{vote:m5}}.

The committee recommended a $1,300,000 in-year budget increase for paramedic compensation and benefits, shared between the City and the County, with the City share paid from the Tax Operating Contingency Reserve.
The committee recommended advancing future budget for replacement ambulances and one growth ambulance into 2025 so vehicles can be ordered early.
The committee recommended advancing the $5,000,000 Central Station electric bus charging budget to 2025, funded by a federal transit grant and a City reserve fund.
The committee received the report on WSIB impacts for emergency services and forwarded it to the Joint Social Services and Land Ambulance Committee for information.
The committee received the value for money audit of facilities cleaning and directed staff to build its recommendations into their workplans.

debate: On the tax subclass, one councillor said the report did not show the effect on other taxpayers and was uneasy backing it without that. Staff said uptake cannot be predicted and the matter is a policy choice, but offered a scenario memo.
Staff explained that the discount would only apply to units with a government agreement. They said annual tax policy reports would show the assessment in the subclass and the discount.

On WSIB, councillors asked whether the reserve is healthy. Staff said it may be below target and would be reviewed in the 2026 budget update. Paramedic staff described difficulty recruiting part-time paramedics to cover absences, since neighbouring services compete for graduates.

On graffiti, the mayor revised the motion to ask for options rather than a draft by-law. Staff said the report fits current resources, but a by-law and faster removal would need budget and could displace other work. Councillors raised mural art, prevention through design, and water use for pressure washing.
